title: Correcting Connectivity in Arc-Based QUBO Models for Fixed-Fleet Vehicle Routing
authors: Omer Gurevich, Maor Matityahu, Tal Mor, Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy
abstract: We revisit a degree-only arc Hamiltonian for fixed-fleet, homogeneous, uncapacitated vehicle routing. Because its local penalties define only a cycle cover, ground states may contain customer cycles disconnected from the depot. We construct a polynomial-size quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) repair using capped single-commodity flow and prove that every ground-state routing is connected and cost-optimal under explicit penalty assumptions. For $N-1$ customers and $K$ nonempty routes, the unreduced encoding uses exactly $|E|(1+\lceil\log_2(N-K+1)\rceil)$ logical problem qubits. A reversible compute--phase--uncompute realization evaluates the flow penalties in $O(N^2\log N+N\log^2N)$ logical gates on a complete graph with $O(\log N)$ reusable workspace and no product register. On complete loopless graphs, a depot-delimited single-sequence position encoding uses fewer problem qubits and fewer written terms when the flow-word length grows. Conversely, the flow model achieves a smaller structured logical-gate upper bound under a common reversible accounting model. Exact audits of the Hamiltonian and circuit implementation, combined with a $1{,}200$-matrix classical benchmark, verify the formulation and quantify the connectivity gap. Finally, a 32,000-shot Amazon Braket task on IQM Emerald characterizes depth-one termwise Ising circuits on a diagnostic $N = 4,\, K = 1$ counterexample instance. In the degree-only circuit, $78.05\%$ of selected $p=1$ shots realize the invalid disconnected ground state; the reduced 14-qubit flow-augmented circuit yields no fully feasible sample. These device results characterize mapped Hamiltonians and compilation rather than an asymptotic routing solution advantage.
summary: This work develops a mathematically rigorous method to correct connectivity flaws in QUBO models designed for the Vehicle Routing Problem. By incorporating a single-commodity flow repair into the Hamiltonian, the authors guarantee that the lowest energy state corresponds to a valid, connected route. The research combines theoretical proof with hardware benchmarking to characterize the feasibility of mapping complex combinatorial problems onto quantum processors.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical issue of ensuring global connectivity in QUBO models used for the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP), where initial formulations only enforce local cycle covers.
main_result: The authors construct and prove a polynomial-size QUBO repair using capped single-commodity flow that guarantees the ground state corresponds to a connected and cost-optimal routing.
method: The methodology involves reformulating the VRP constraints into a flow-augmented QUBO, followed by resource analysis (qubits, gates) and benchmarking on quantum hardware simulators and actual quantum processors.
model_or_system: The system is the fixed-fleet, homogeneous, uncapacitated VRP, modeled using an arc-based QUBO Hamiltonian. The core challenge is augmenting the Hamiltonian to enforce single-commodity flow constraints to guarantee connectivity.
key_observables: Connectivity gap, logical problem qubits required, number of written Hamiltonian interactions, and the probability of observing disconnected ground states on quantum hardware.
important_parameters: Number of customers (N), number of routes (K), and the size of the graph (E).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the VRP is fixed-fleet, homogeneous, and uncapacitated. The quantum results are explicitly stated to characterize compilation limitations rather than asymptotic algorithmic advantages.
figures_summary: The notes mention a counterexample (N=6, K=1) illustrating the cost difference between disconnected cycle covers and valid Hamiltonian cycles, and references to resource scaling comparisons between flow-augmented and position-indexed encodings.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the connectivity failure in degree-only arc Hamiltonians, proposes the flow-augmented QUBO repair, analyzes the resource scaling and theoretical guarantees, and concludes with experimental characterization on quantum hardware using diagnostic counterexamples.
why_interesting: It directly tackles the gap between theoretical QUBO formulation and physical realizability by providing a rigorous method to enforce global constraints (connectivity) necessary for complex combinatorial optimization problems on quantum hardware.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
